en: He came to work even though he had a fever.
why: にもかかわらず follows the plain verb ある, and {出勤|しゅっきん} goes right before した.

before: {明日|あした}は{大事|だいじ}な{会議|かいぎ}があるので、
en: I have an important meeting tomorrow, so I can't take the day off.
why: The set pattern is verb + わけにはいかない.

before: {上司|じょうし}に{頼|たの}まれたら、
en: If my boss asks me, I will have no choice but to accept.
why: The pattern is verb stem (ない-form) + ざるを{得|え}ない.

before: {部屋|へや}の{電気|でんき}がついているから、{彼|かれ}はもう
en: The light in his room is on, so he must have already come home.
why: {帰|かえ}ってきた is one verb, then に{違|ちが}いない closes it.

after: {日本語|にほんご}を{勉強|べんきょう}し{始|はじ}めた。
en: Japanese anime got me started studying Japanese.
why: {日本|にほん}の modifies アニメ, and the pattern is noun + をきっかけに.

en: Please carry out the work according to the plan we decided last week.
why: {先週|せんしゅう}{決|き}めた modifies {計画|けいかく}, and に{沿|そ}って follows the noun.

before: {彼女|かのじょ}は{英語|えいご}
en: I hear she can speak not only English but French too.
why: ばかりか attaches to {英語|えいご}, then the second item takes も before the verb.

en: Far from saving money, my debt went up.
why: どころか follows the verb, then a subject with が and the て-form before しまった.

before: {車|くるま}の{免許|めんきょ}は
en: I got my driving license, but I have never driven even once.
why: ものの follows {取|と}った, and {一度|いちど}も needs the negative verb {運転|うんてん}していない.

en: If you keep pushing yourself like this, you could ruin your health.
why: {無理|むり}を needs a verb ({続|つづ}ける), and かねない follows the stem {壊|こわ}し.

before: {申|もう}し{訳|わけ}ありませんが、その
en: I'm sorry, but I'm unable to answer that question.
why: その modifies ご{質問|しつもん}, には marks it, and お{答|こた}えしかねます is the polite refusal.

before: この{会社|かいしゃ}では、{社員|しゃいん}は{毎朝|まいあさ}
en: At this company, staff are supposed to arrive by nine every morning.
why: までに follows the time, and ことになっている follows the plain verb.

en: This shop is full of customers not only on weekends but on weekdays too.
why: に{限|かぎ}らず follows the first noun, and も marks the second one.

after: お{寺|てら}がたくさんある。
en: Kyoto has many famous temples, starting with Kinkaku-ji.
why: The pattern is noun + をはじめ, and {有名|ゆうめい}な must sit right before お{寺|てら}.

after: {目|め}が{覚|さ}めるようになった。
en: As I get older, I have started waking up early in the morning.
why: {年|とし}を needs {取|と}る, につれて follows it, and {朝|あさ}{早|はや}く is a fixed phrase.

en: Along with the population increase, housing has become scarce.
why: {人口|じんこう}の modifies {増加|ぞうか}, に{伴|ともな}って follows it, and が marks the new subject.

en: Please sign after reading the contract carefully.
why: よく modifies {読|よ}んだ, {上|うえ}で follows the た-form, and サイン goes before して.

en: We will contact you as soon as we know the details.
why: {次第|しだい} follows the verb stem {分|わ}かり, and ご{連絡|れんらく} goes right before いたします.

en: I want to go to many countries while I'm young.
why: うちに follows {若|わか}い, いろいろな modifies {国|くに}, and {行|い}って comes before みたい.

en: You can't tell what kind of person someone is without actually meeting and talking to them.
why: ないことには follows the negative verb, and the question どんな{人|ひと}か goes before {分|わ}からない.

en: Just because something is expensive doesn't mean the quality is good.
why: からといって follows {高|たか}い, and the clause {品質|ひんしつ}がいい comes before とは{限|かぎ}らない.

after: が、{時間|じかん}がなくてできない。
en: It's not that I dislike cooking, but I have no time to do it.
why: The pattern is {嫌|きら}いな + わけではない.

before: その{映画|えいが}の{最後|さいご}を{見|み}て、
en: Watching the end of that movie, I couldn't help crying.
why: The pattern is ない-stem {泣|な}か + ずにはいられない.

before: {住所|じゅうしょ}も{電話番号|でんわばんごう}も{分|わ}からないので、
en: I don't know his address or phone number, so there's no way to contact him.
why: ようがない follows the verb stem し of {連絡|れんらく}する.

en: If I could go back, I would go back to my student days.
why: ものなら follows the potential verb, and {学生|がくせい}{時代|じだい}に is the place to return to.

before: {昨日|きのう}あまり{寝|ね}ていないので、
en: I didn't sleep much yesterday, so I'm terribly sleepy today.
why: The pattern is adjective て-form {眠|ねむ}くて + しょうがない.

en: Anyone who has an opinion on this problem, please raise your hand.
why: この modifies {問題|もんだい}, に{関|かん}して follows it, and ご{意見|いけん}のある modifies {方|かた}.

en: Customs differ depending on the country or region.
why: によって follows the noun, then {習慣|しゅうかん}が is the subject of {違|ちが}う.

after: ので、お{腹|なか}がすいた。
en: I went out today without breakfast, so I'm hungry.
why: The pattern is noun + {抜|ぬ}きで, then the verb before ので.

en: This movie was made based on a true story.
why: {本当|ほんとう}にあった modifies {話|はなし}, and をもとに follows the noun.

en: The fee changes according to the time used.
why: {使|つか}った modifies {時間|じかん}, に{応|おう}じて follows it, and {変|か}わり takes ます.

en: My brother does nothing himself, yet he only complains.
why: {何|なに}も needs the negative しない, くせに follows it, and {文句|もんく} goes before ばかり{言|い}う.

before: {都会|とかい}の{生活|せいかつ}は{便利|べんり}な
after: という{問題|もんだい}もある。
en: City life is convenient, but on the other hand prices are high.
why: {反面|はんめん} follows {便利|べんり}な, then {物価|ぶっか}が{高|たか}い is the new clause.

en: After talking it over many times, I decided to quit the company.
why: {末|すえ}に follows the た-form, and {会社|かいしゃ}を{辞|や}める comes before ことにした.

en: After agonizing for three hours, I came home without buying anything.
why: あげく follows the た-form, and {何|なに}も needs the negative {買|か}わずに.

en: Since I promised, I can't not keep it.
why: {以上|いじょう} follows {約束|やくそく}した, then the pattern ないわけにはいかない.

after: しっかり{身|み}につけたい。
en: Since I'm studying abroad, I want to properly learn the local language.
why: からには follows the verb, and {現地|げんち}の modifies {言葉|ことば}.

en: Thanks to my teacher teaching me carefully, I passed.
why: {丁寧|ていねい}に modifies {教|おし}えて, then くれた, then おかげで.

en: Because I overslept, I missed my usual train.
why: せいで follows the た-form, いつもの modifies {電車|でんしゃ}, and {乗|の}り joins {遅|おく}れた.

before: {簡単|かんたん}な{手術|しゅじゅつ}だから、そんなに
en: It's a simple operation, so there's no need to worry that much.
why: The pattern is verb + ことはない.

en: Winter is cold, so I tend to shut myself up at home.
why: がち follows the verb stem, and になる closes it.

en: This is a book written for children.
why: {向|む}けに follows {子|こ}ども, and {書|か}かれた modifies {本|ほん}.

before: この{店|みせ}の{料理|りょうり}は
en: The food at this shop is tasty for the price.
why: The pattern is noun + のわりに, then the adjective.

en: On my way to the station, I stopped by a bookshop.
why: {駅|えき}へ needs {行|い}く, ついでに follows it, and {寄|よ}って comes before きた.

en: Every time I hear this song, I remember my hometown.
why: たびに follows {聞|き}く, and {故郷|こきょう}の modifies こと.

en: My phone rang in the middle of the meeting.
why: {会議|かいぎ}の modifies {最中|さいちゅう}, then {携帯|けいたい}が is the subject of {鳴|な}ってしまった.

before: {急|きゅう}に{車|くるま}が{出|で}てきて、もう{少|すこ}しで
en: A car suddenly came out, and I nearly had an accident.
why: {事故|じこ}に{遭|あ}う is one phrase, and ところだった follows the plain verb.

before: あんなに{練習|れんしゅう}したのだから、{彼女|かのじょ}が
en: She practiced so much, so she is sure to win the match.
why: {試合|しあい}に goes with {勝|か}つ, and に{決|き}まっている follows the plain verb.

en: Just because I told the truth, I ended up fighting with my friend.
why: ばかりに follows {言|い}った, and {友達|ともだち}と goes with けんかになった.

en: If you just take the medicine, your cold will get better soon.
why: The pattern is stem + さえすれば, then {風邪|かぜ}は starts the result.
